description: Checkpoint receipt of consistency KAT over the canonical 39-node MMR: tree, size-driven fold (consistent_roots_for_sizes), rejected proof shapes, protected-header classes (ADR-0066 D9), and signed receipts under fixed test keys.

conventions.sizes: node counts; MMR(size) has size nodes; tree_size_1 = 0 is the empty origin
conventions.protected_header: deterministic CBOR map {1: alg, 395: 3, -65933: tree_size_2}, keys ordered shorter-encoding-first then bytewise
conventions.detached_payload: raw concatenation of the accumulator peaks of tree_size_2, descending height, no framing
conventions.es256: ECDSA P-256 over sha256(sig_structure); signature r||s, 64 bytes, low-s
conventions.ks256: ECDSA secp256k1 over keccak256(sig_structure); signature r||s||v, 65 bytes, v in {27, 28}; verifier recovers the address
conventions.receipt: CBOR tag 18 [bstr(protected), {396: {-2: bstr(consistency_proof)}}, null, bstr(signature)]; the single-proof form the receipts and receipt_negatives rows carry, and the form of every checkpoint sealed before the array form
conventions.receipt_chain: CBOR tag 18 [bstr(protected), {396: {-2: [bstr(consistency_proof), ...]}}, null, bstr(signature)]; the draft's consistency-proofs = [ + consistency-proof ], one proof per sealed step in fold order, carried by the receipt_chains rows. An empty array is not a receipt of consistency and is rejected. A verifier accepts both forms; a producer writes this one
conventions.consistency_proof: bstr(CBOR [tree_size_1, tree_size_2, [[bstr path node]...], [bstr right peak]...])

tree.interior_rule: sha256(BE8(pos)) || left || right) with pos = mmr_index + 1 (hash_pospair64)

consistency_negatives.name: incomplete-tree-size/7-to-9
consistency_negatives.mutation: tree_size_2 set to 9, which is not a complete MMR size

consistency_negatives.name: peak-count-mismatch/7-to-15-missing-peak
consistency_negatives.mutation: last accumulator entry and its path removed

consistency_negatives.name: path-length-mismatch/1-to-3-empty-path
consistency_negatives.mutation: the single path emptied; sizes imply length 1

consistency_negatives.name: path-length-mismatch/7-to-15-lengthened
consistency_negatives.mutation: one node appended to every path

consistency_negatives.name: root-mismatch/10-to-15-altered-sibling
consistency_negatives.mutation: first sibling of the second path zeroed; two paths under one target peak prove different roots

consistency_negatives.name: right-peak-count-mismatch/7-to-8-surplus
consistency_negatives.mutation: an extra right peak supplied; the sizes fix the count at 1

consistency_negatives.name: base-mismatch/declared-4-trusted-7
consistency_negatives.mutation: proof declares tree_size_1 = 4 while the verifier's trusted size is 7; the verifier compares and rejects before folding

protected_headers.name: canonical/size-8
protected_headers.note: the sealer's ES256 header, size 8 as a 1-byte uint

protected_headers.name: canonical/size-2^40-8-byte-arg
protected_headers.note: size 2^40 needs an 8-byte argument; accepted by the header parser (the fold rejects it later as incomplete). Kept below 2^53 so every JSON consumer reads it exactly

protected_headers.name: skip/mt7-half-float-1.0
protected_headers.note: {7: 1.0} as a half float, its shortest form

protected_headers.name: skip/mt7-half-nan
protected_headers.note: {7: NaN} as a half float, its shortest form

protected_headers.name: skip/mt7-double-float-1e300
protected_headers.note: {7: 1e300}; no shorter form preserves the value

protected_headers.name: skip/two-unread-labels-length-first-order
protected_headers.note: keys 1, -1 (0x20), 24 (0x1818), 395, -65933 in length-first order; -1 (1 byte) precedes 24 (2 bytes) although 0x18 < 0x20 bytewise

protected_headers.name: absent/no-tree-size-label
protected_headers.note: {1: -7, 395: 3}: the pre-ADR-0066 header; no signed size

protected_headers.name: reject/mt7-simple-40
protected_headers.note: {7: simple(40)}; only false, true and null are allowed

protected_headers.name: reject/mt7-single-float-1.0
protected_headers.note: 1.0 as a single; a half preserves the value

protected_headers.name: reject/mt7-double-nan
protected_headers.note: NaN as a double; the half form preserves it

protected_headers.name: reject/invalid-utf8-under-unread-label
protected_headers.note: {7: tstr(0xff)}; text strings must be valid UTF-8

protected_headers.name: reject/two-unread-labels-bytewise-order
protected_headers.note: keys 1, 24 (0x1818), -1 (0x20), 395, -65933: bytewise order (0x18 < 0x20) is not length-first order

protected_headers.name: reject/under-declared-map
protected_headers.note: map(2) carrying three pairs; the third is trailing

protected_headers.name: reject/mt7-truncated-float
protected_headers.note: half float cut off by the header end

receipt_negatives.name: reject/signed-size-10-declared-8
receipt_negatives.note: the signature verifies over {..., -65933: 10} and this payload; the proof's tree_size_2 is 8

receipt_negatives.name: reject/replay-7-to-8-declared-7-to-10
receipt_negatives.note: the FOR-568 substitution: byte-identical paths, right peak and signature, tree_size_2 declared 10; sizes 8 and 10 both take one right peak so the fold accepts either, and only the signed size rejects it

receipt_negatives.name: reject/signed-size-absent
receipt_negatives.note: a valid pre-ADR-0066 receipt: {1: -7, 395: 3} signed over the same payload

receipt_negatives.name: reject/payload-is-hashed-accumulator
receipt_negatives.note: signed over sha256(peaks) instead of the raw concatenation (ADR-0046)

receipt_negatives.name: reject/es256-high-s
receipt_negatives.note: mathematically valid ECDSA with s > n/2; verifiers require low-s

receipt_chains.name: accept/chain-1-3-4-7
receipt_chains.note: three sealed steps relayed under one signature; folding them in order from the accumulator of size 1 reaches the accumulator of size 7, which is the detached payload

receipt_chains.name: reject/chain-middle-step-off-by-one
receipt_chains.note: the first step ends at size 3 and the second declares size 2 as its origin; the paths and the signature are the genuine ones, and only the comparison with the previous step rejects it

receipt_chains.name: reject/chain-signed-size-is-an-intermediate-step
receipt_chains.note: a genuine receipt for 1 -> 4 with the 4 -> 7 step appended under its signature; the signed tree-size-2 is 4 where the last step declares 7, so the accumulator the chain reaches is unsigned
